description: Three sawtooth oscillators stacked into one fat voice, each detuned and shaped on its own, with a control that locks the second and third to the first

params.text: Sets the pitch of all three in whole octaves, three either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Bends that oscillator's sawtooth: turned one way the ramp is pushed down toward the floor for most of the cycle, and the other way it is pulled up toward the ceiling
Detunes that oscillator, an octave either way
Forces the second and third oscillators onto the first one's phase for as long as it is held, which locks the three together and thins the sound

inputs.text: Sets the pitch of all three, an octave per volt, added to the OCTAVE knob and held within four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Moves that oscillator's shape, an octave of the shape range for every 5V, added to its knob
Detunes that oscillator, an octave for every 5V, added to its knob
Any voltage other than 0V here forces the second and third oscillators onto the first one's phase

outputs.text: The three oscillators added together and scaled back down

notes: the three oscillators drift apart on their own when the align control is released, since nothing else holds their phases together.
with all three tune knobs at centre and align off, the three oscillators are at the same frequency and slowly beat against each other from wherever their phases happen to be.
the shape control mixes three curves: a fourth power, the plain ramp, and a ninth root; the plain ramp is what the knob gives at its centre.
the output is the sum of the three divided by three and scaled to about ±5V, so muting two of them does not make the third louder.

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
